anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves f5 to holds: it names the 12:15:00 deadline against the 12:15:01 clock, ties non-renewal explicitly to the absence of an own push since 12:00 and the non-counting 12:10 base observation, runs no watch, and renders an obstacle menu whose deliver row promises exactly one more 15-minute window with no round charged and neither cap extended, while no ordinary wait row appears. Before failed because it still rendered a generic `wait` as row 1 (ordinary wait present) and offered no numeric deliver continuation, and it also disowned the retained course and caps as undefined schema fields. Keep After's wording; one tightening worth considering is the assess row, which says 'then approve or stop' on the viewer's own PR — approve is never offered to the author, so phrasing it as 'then stop' (or 'nothing posts; stop') would avoid implying an approval path while leaving the obstacle template, deliver-one-window semantics and cap-freeze language intact.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After delivers the Change for this case: it recognizes the expired deadline (12:15:01Z past 12:15:00Z, established at the last own push with the 12:10 base observation not renewing it), refuses `gh pr checks --watch` and any renewal, exits the course with `stuck - CI pending past 15 minutes`, renders the obstacle template, and offers a numeric `deliver` row that explicitly opens exactly one additional 15-minute window while stating neither cap increases, with no ordinary `wait` row and stop recommended last. Before failed f5 because it rendered `Verdict: fixable`, offered `wait` as the recommended row, offered no numeric deliver continuation, and never named the timeout as an obstacle. Nothing in After regressed relative to Before on this fact; to keep it stable, retain the explicit sentence that the timeout continuation opens one window and extends neither cap, keep show evidence as a hint rather than a numeric row, and keep `wait` out of the obstacle menu.
